title: Interactive artifact lifecycle and residency orchestration
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers need fine-grained controls for how long interactive artifacts (prompts, model responses, request logs, derived metrics) live, where they are stored, and how we produce tamper-evident evidence bundles for audits. Current system has per-tenant TTLs but lacks: (1) per-route/operation TTL overrides, (2) clear residency mapping for multi-region tenants, (3) a preview/impact UI for purges, and (4) an automated snapshot/attestation flow for compliance reviewers. This ticket scopes a cross-functional plan to add: - Per-route lifecycle policy objects with inheritance from tenant defaults - Residency hints and enforcement during write time + post-hoc reassignment for region-bound artifacts - Soft-snapshot API that produces signed evidence bundles (manifest + hashes + minimal sample sets) for a time window - Console preview and API to simulate purge outcomes and storage cost delta - Sampling rules for metrics/telemetry to avoid retention cost explosion while preserving auditability Goals: - Enable legal & infosec to request auditable evidence per compliance request within SLA - Give engineering and product teams tools to control cost vs fidelity trade-offs per route - Make retention changes observable, reversible (soft-delete), and verifiable by third parties
acceptance_criteria: API: Create/Update/Delete lifecycle policy (per-tenant, per-route) and return effective TTL and residency for a given route
Write-path: Incoming request records include residency tag; runtime rejects writes if tenant disallows region
Snapshot API: /v1/tenants/{t}/evidence/snapshot produces a signed ZIP with manifest, per-item hashes, and minimal redaction when requested
Console: Preview purge UI shows sample percentage of affected artifacts and estimated cost savings
Metrics: Sampling config per-route for telemetry retained for audits, with immutable audit-log entry of sampling decisions
Security: Attestation bundles are signed by KMS and include chain-of-custody headers
Tests: End-to-end test validating purge simulation, snapshot creation, and verification using test KMS key
tasks: PM: Finalize policy DSL and UI language (TTL, residency, sample_rate, snapshot_policy)
Design: Wireframes for Console purge preview and lifecycle policy editor (DES task)
ENG: Schema changes for lifecycle_policy on route objects + enforcement in write path (ENG-XXXXX)
ENG: Implement soft-snapshot export service with streaming hash computation and KMS signing (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4567)
ENG: Add residency enforcement middleware to runtime and a post-ingest reassignment job
Security: Threat model & review for snapshot and export flow
PM: Prepare compliance playbook and customer-facing docs describing guarantees and expected evidence artifacts (Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/GOV/Interactive+Artifact+Lifecycle)
notes: Trade-offs discussed: strong per-route retention increases storage costs; sampling mitigates cost but reduces completeness — default is tenant-level high-fidelity for legal routes and sampled for analytics routes.
Decision: Use 'soft-delete' period of 7 days as safety window before hard purge to allow for fast restores and forensic captures.
Residency mapping will use geo-hints at write-time and a nightly reconciler to meet contractual residency guarantees for existing artifacts.
We will expose a dry-run API for purge operations that returns example object keys and an estimated byte count; actual purge requires two-phase commit from Console or API.
Legal asked for chain-of-custody fields: capture actor, timestamp, request_id, rationale for snapshot exports. Will include in manifest.
Initial KMS integration will use existing platform keyring; plan to add customer-managed keys in a follow-up (Private offering).
